header:
How to pick investments
in your 401(k)

lines.text: In 2025, 61% of Vanguard savers held one target-date fund.
lines.say: In twenty twenty-five, sixty-one percent of Vanguard savers held one target-date fund.

lines.text: Nothing else: their whole balance sat in that one fund, per Vanguard's How America Saves 2026.
lines.say: Nothing else. Their whole balance sat in that one fund, according to Vanguard's How America Saves twenty twenty-six.

lines.text: So is that lazy, or the whole point? Stick around, and you'll see exactly what's inside that one fund.
lines.say: So is that lazy, or the whole point? Stick around, and you'll see exactly what's inside that one fund.

lines.text: When you join a 401(k), you get a menu of funds, and most people have no idea what they're ordering.
lines.say: When you join a four-oh-one-K, you get a menu of funds, and most people have no idea what they're ordering.

lines.text: Here's the plan: what's on the menu, what it costs, how the mix works, and the 2026 rules.
lines.say: Here's the plan: what's on the menu, what it costs, how the mix works, and the twenty twenty-six rules.

lines.text: This is education, not advice. I won't tell you what to pick. I'll show you how the options work.
lines.say: This is education, not advice. I won't tell you what to pick. I'll show you how the options work.

lines.text: Chapter 1: What's on the menu.
lines.say: Chapter one: what's on the menu.

lines.text: A 401(k) is an account, not an investment. Every dollar you put in has to land in a fund your plan offers.
lines.say: A four-oh-one-K is an account, not an investment. Every dollar you put in has to land in a fund your plan offers.

lines.text: Your employer builds the menu and picks a default. You choose from that menu and set your own mix.
lines.say: Your employer builds the menu and picks a default. You choose from that menu and set your own mix.

lines.text: And if you never choose? Your money still gets invested. It goes into the plan's default fund.
lines.say: And if you never choose? Your money still gets invested. It goes straight into the plan's default fund.

lines.text: The Labor Department's rule calls that a qualified default investment alternative, or QDIA.
lines.say: The Labor Department's rule calls that a qualified default investment alternative, or Q D I A.

lines.text: Under that rule, a QDIA can be a target-date fund, a balanced fund, or a managed account.
lines.say: Under that rule, a Q D I A can be a target-date fund, a balanced fund, or a managed account.

lines.text: There's a fourth, a capital preservation option, but only for the first 120 days after your first contribution.
lines.say: There's also a fourth, a capital preservation option, but only for the first hundred and twenty days after your first contribution.

lines.text: Defaults matter even more under SECURE 2.0: most 401(k) plans set up after Dec. 29, 2022 must auto-enroll workers from 2025.
lines.say: Defaults matter even more under SECURE two point oh. Most four-oh-one-K plans set up after December twenty-ninth, twenty twenty-two must auto-enroll workers, starting in twenty twenty-five.

lines.text: Those plans start you at 3% to 10% of pay, then add 1 point a year until you reach at least 10%, capped at 15%.
lines.say: Those plans start you at three to ten percent of pay, then add one point a year until you reach at least ten percent, capped at fifteen.

lines.text: And at the end of 2025, 61% of Vanguard plans used automatic enrollment. Yes, 61% again. Coincidence.
lines.say: And at the end of twenty twenty-five, sixty-one percent of Vanguard plans used automatic enrollment. Yes, sixty-one percent again. Pure coincidence.

lines.text: Each plan spells out its default in required notices, including the QDIA notice.
lines.say: Each plan spells out its default in required notices, including the Q D I A notice.

lines.text: The menu itself could change, too. In March 2026, the Labor Department proposed a rule on how plans pick their funds.
lines.say: The menu itself could change, too. In March twenty twenty-six, the Labor Department proposed a rule on how plans pick their funds.

lines.text: It aims to make alternatives like private equity and crypto easier to add. As of early October 2026, it was still a proposal.
lines.say: It aims to make alternatives like private equity and crypto easier to add. As of early October twenty twenty-six, it was still a proposal.

lines.text: Chapter 2: The one-fund option.
lines.say: Chapter two: the one-fund option.

lines.text: The most common default is a target-date fund, and 96% of Vanguard plans offered one at the end of 2025.
lines.say: The most common default is a target-date fund, and ninety-six percent of Vanguard plans offered one at the end of twenty twenty-five.

lines.text: The year in the name is roughly the retirement year. Someone born in 1996 turns 65 in 2061.
lines.say: The year in the name is roughly the retirement year. Someone born in nineteen ninety-six turns sixty-five in twenty sixty-one.

lines.text: Inside is a whole portfolio: US stocks, international stocks and bonds, all wrapped in one fund.
lines.say: Inside is a whole portfolio: US stocks, international stocks and bonds, all wrapped up in one fund.

lines.text: The key feature is the glide path. The mix starts mostly in stocks and shifts toward bonds as the target year gets closer.
lines.say: The key feature is the glide path. The mix starts out mostly in stocks and shifts toward bonds as the target year gets closer.

lines.text: One catch: two 2060 funds from different companies can hold very different mixes. Same year, different recipe.
lines.say: One catch: two twenty sixty funds from different companies can hold very different mixes. Same year, different recipe.

lines.text: Another catch: a target-date fund is built to be the whole portfolio. Stack other funds on top, and the overall mix changes.
lines.say: Another catch: a target-date fund is built to be the whole portfolio. Stack other funds on top of it, and the overall mix changes.

lines.text: Morningstar says the average target-date mutual fund charged 0.27% in 2025, down from 0.29% in 2024.
lines.say: Morningstar says the average target-date mutual fund charged zero point two seven percent in twenty twenty-five, down from zero point two nine in twenty twenty-four.

lines.text: And Morningstar found index-based target-date series cost about 0.53 percentage points less than active-based ones, on average.
lines.say: And Morningstar found index-based target-date series cost about zero point five three percentage points less than active-based ones, on average.

lines.text: So that's why one fund is so common: it's often the default, it's diversified, and it adjusts with age on its own.
lines.say: So that's why one fund is so common: it's often the default, it's already diversified, and it adjusts with age on its own.

lines.text: The trade-off is control. You get the fund company's mix and glide path, not one built around your situation.
lines.say: The trade-off is control. You get the fund company's mix and glide path, not one built around your situation.

lines.text: Chapter 3: Building your own mix.
lines.say: Chapter three: building your own mix.

lines.text: Skip the target-date fund, and the menu usually offers building blocks. Here are four you'll often see, starting with index funds.
lines.say: Skip the target-date fund, and the menu usually offers building blocks. Here are four you'll often see, starting with index funds.

lines.text: An index fund simply copies a market index, like the S&P 500 or the whole US bond market. Nobody picks stocks.
lines.say: An index fund simply copies a market index, like the S and P five hundred or the whole US bond market. Nobody's picking stocks.

lines.text: That keeps costs low. ICI found index stock mutual funds averaged 0.05% a year in 2025.
lines.say: That keeps costs low. The Investment Company Institute, or I C I, found index stock mutual funds averaged zero point zero five percent a year in twenty twenty-five.

lines.text: Actively managed funds pay a team to pick investments and try to beat an index.
lines.say: Actively managed funds pay a team to pick investments and try to beat an index.

lines.text: That costs more. Actively managed US stock mutual funds averaged 0.64% in 2025, per ICI.
lines.say: That costs more. Actively managed US stock mutual funds averaged zero point six four percent in twenty twenty-five, per I C I.

lines.text: Some active funds beat their index in a given stretch, and some don't. Either way, the fee comes out every single year.
lines.say: Some active funds beat their index in a given stretch, and some don't. Either way, the fee comes out every single year.

lines.text: Next up is stable value, a conservative option you'll mostly find in workplace plans.
lines.say: Next up is stable value, a conservative option you'll mostly find in workplace plans.

lines.text: It usually holds bonds wrapped in insurance contracts, which smooth out the bumps and credit a steady interest rate.
lines.say: It usually holds bonds wrapped in insurance contracts, which smooth out the bumps and credit a steady interest rate.

lines.text: The trade-offs: it's built for steadiness, not big growth, and some plans limit moving money from it into similar cash-like funds.
lines.say: The trade-offs: it's built for steadiness, not big growth, and some plans limit moving money from it into similar cash-like funds.

lines.text: The last block is company stock, meaning shares of the company you work for.
lines.say: The last block is company stock, meaning shares of the company you actually work for.

lines.text: Here's the risk: your paycheck and your savings ride on one company. If it struggles, both can take a hit.
lines.say: Here's the risk: your paycheck and your savings ride on one company. If it struggles, both can take a hit.

lines.text: The law builds in an exit. In plans holding public company stock, shares bought with your own money can be moved out from day one.
lines.say: The law builds in an exit. In plans holding public company stock, shares bought with your own money can be moved out from day one.

lines.text: For shares from employer contributions, that right kicks in after 3 years of service.
lines.say: For shares that came from employer contributions, that right kicks in after three years of service.

lines.text: That's tax code section 401(a)(35), and plans have to let people make that switch at least quarterly.
lines.say: That's tax code section four-oh-one A thirty-five, and plans have to let people make that switch at least quarterly.

lines.text: Chapter 4: What fees really cost.
lines.say: Chapter four: what fees really cost.

lines.text: Every fund has an expense ratio: the percent of your balance the fund keeps each year to run itself.
lines.say: Every fund has an expense ratio: the percent of your balance the fund keeps each year to run itself.

lines.text: You never get a bill for it. It comes out of the fund's returns, which is exactly why it's easy to miss.
lines.say: You never get a bill for it. It comes out of the fund's returns, which is exactly why it's so easy to miss.

lines.text: The good news: costs have fallen. In 2000, 401(k) savers in stock mutual funds paid 0.76% a year on average, per ICI.
lines.say: Good news: costs have fallen. In two thousand, four-oh-one-K savers in stock mutual funds paid zero point seven six percent a year on average, per I C I.

lines.text: By 2024 it was 0.26%, a 66% drop, and below the 0.40% paid industrywide.
lines.say: By twenty twenty-four it was zero point two six percent, a sixty-six percent drop, and below the zero point four zero percent paid industrywide.

lines.text: Averages hide big gaps. Hypothetical: $50,000, no new deposits, 30 years, 7% a year before fees. An assumption, not a forecast.
lines.say: Averages hide big gaps, so here's a hypothetical: fifty thousand dollars, no new deposits, thirty years, seven percent a year before fees. That's an assumption, not a forecast.

lines.text: Fund A charges 0.05%, netting 6.95%. Fund B charges 0.75%, netting 6.25%.
lines.say: Fund A charges zero point zero five percent, netting six point nine five. Fund B charges zero point seven five, netting six point two five.

lines.text: In year one, that's $25 versus $375 in fees. Annoying, but not life-changing, right?
lines.say: In year one, that's twenty-five dollars versus three hundred seventy-five dollars in fees. Annoying, but not life-changing, right?

lines.text: Compound it for 30 years, and Fund A grows to $375,313.
lines.say: Compound it for thirty years, and Fund A grows to three hundred seventy-five thousand, three hundred thirteen dollars.

lines.text: Fund B grows to $308,204.
lines.say: Fund B grows to three hundred eight thousand, two hundred four dollars.

lines.text: Same money, same market, and a gap of $67,109 that comes purely from fees.
lines.say: Same money, same market, and a gap of sixty-seven thousand, one hundred nine dollars that comes purely from fees.

lines.text: And it snowballs, because fees eat the growth on the growth. The gap is $6,222 after 10 years.
lines.say: And it snowballs, because fees eat the growth on the growth. The gap is six thousand, two hundred twenty-two dollars after ten years.

lines.text: It's $23,591 after 20 years, so nearly two-thirds of the gap lands in the last 10.
lines.say: It's twenty-three thousand, five hundred ninety-one after twenty years, so nearly two-thirds of the gap lands in the last ten.

lines.text: You don't have to guess. Labor Department rules require a fee disclosure listing every fund's expense ratio.
lines.say: You don't have to guess. Labor Department rules require a fee disclosure listing every fund's expense ratio.

lines.text: Fees aren't everything. But they're one of the few things about a fund you know in advance.
lines.say: Fees aren't everything. But they're one of the few things about a fund you know in advance.

lines.text: Chapter 5: Your mix and rebalancing.
lines.say: Chapter five: your mix, and rebalancing.

lines.text: Picking funds is really picking a mix: how much goes into stocks, and how much into bonds.
lines.say: Picking funds is really picking a mix: how much goes into stocks, and how much goes into bonds.

lines.text: That split is called asset allocation, and it shapes how bumpy the ride feels.
lines.say: That split is called asset allocation, and it shapes how bumpy the ride feels.

lines.text: For a reference point, 79% of contribution dollars at Vanguard went into stocks in 2025.
lines.say: For a reference point, seventy-nine percent of contribution dollars at Vanguard went into stocks in twenty twenty-five.

lines.text: Diversification is the other half: spreading money across many companies, industries and countries.
lines.say: Diversification is the other half: spreading money across many companies, industries and countries.

lines.text: A total market index fund can hold thousands of companies. A company stock fund holds exactly one.
lines.say: A total market index fund can hold thousands of companies. A company stock fund holds exactly one.

lines.text: Then markets move, and the mix drifts. Say, hypothetically, someone sets a target of 80% stocks and 20% bonds.
lines.say: Then markets move, and the mix drifts. Say, hypothetically, someone sets a target of eighty percent stocks and twenty percent bonds.

lines.text: If stocks gain 25% in a year and bonds stay flat, that drifts to about 83/17, with nobody touching a thing.
lines.say: If stocks gain twenty-five percent in a year and bonds stay flat, that drifts to about eighty-three seventeen, with nobody touching a thing.

lines.text: Rebalancing means bringing it back to the target, and there are a few common ways people do it.
lines.say: Rebalancing means bringing it back to the target, and there are a few common ways people do it.

lines.text: Some plans offer automatic rebalancing on a schedule, and target-date funds handle it inside the fund.
lines.say: Some plans offer automatic rebalancing on a schedule, and target-date funds handle it inside the fund.

lines.text: And trades inside a 401(k) don't create a tax bill. With traditional money, tax comes when you withdraw.
lines.say: And trades inside a four-oh-one-K don't create a tax bill. With traditional money, the tax comes when you withdraw.

lines.text: Chapter 6: 2026 limits and the match.
lines.say: Chapter six: twenty twenty-six limits, and the match.

lines.text: Now, how much can go in. For 2026, the IRS limit on what employees put in is $24,500.
lines.say: Now, how much can go in. For twenty twenty-six, the I R S limit on what employees put in is twenty-four thousand, five hundred dollars.

lines.text: It keeps climbing. Back in 2006, the limit was $15,000.
lines.say: It keeps climbing. Back in two thousand six, the limit was fifteen thousand dollars.

lines.text: That's $9,500 more room in 2026 than in 2006.
lines.say: That's nine thousand, five hundred dollars more room in twenty twenty-six than in two thousand six.

lines.text: If you're 50 or older, there's an $8,000 catch-up on top, for $32,500 total.
lines.say: If you're fifty or older, there's an eight thousand dollar catch-up on top, for thirty-two thousand, five hundred total.

lines.text: Turning 60 through 63 in 2026? The super catch-up is $11,250, if the plan offers it.
lines.say: Turning sixty through sixty-three in twenty twenty-six? The super catch-up is eleven thousand, two hundred fifty dollars, if the plan offers it.

lines.text: New for 2026: if your 2025 FICA wages from that employer topped $150,000, catch-up money has to go in as Roth.
lines.say: New for twenty twenty-six: if your twenty twenty-five FICA wages from that employer topped a hundred and fifty thousand dollars, catch-up money has to go in as Roth.

lines.text: Roth means after-tax now, and tax-free later if the rules are met. It only applies to the catch-up part.
lines.say: Roth means after-tax now, and tax-free later if the rules are met. It only applies to the catch-up part.

lines.text: One more ceiling: employee plus employer money together can't top $72,000 in 2026, not counting catch-ups.
lines.say: One more ceiling: employee plus employer money together can't top seventy-two thousand dollars in twenty twenty-six, not counting catch-ups.

lines.text: Now, the match. Plenty of employers add money when you contribute, for example 50 cents per dollar, up to 6% of pay.
lines.say: Now, the match. Plenty of employers add money when you contribute, for example fifty cents for every dollar, up to six percent of pay.

lines.text: Worked example: on a $60,000 salary, 6% is $3,600. A 50% match on that adds $1,800 a year.
lines.say: Worked example: on a sixty thousand dollar salary, six percent is three thousand, six hundred dollars. A fifty percent match on that adds eighteen hundred dollars a year.

lines.text: But matched money might not be fully yours yet. That's called vesting.
lines.say: But matched money might not be fully yours yet. That's called vesting.

lines.text: Your own contributions are always 100% yours. Employer money can follow a schedule.
lines.say: Your own contributions are always one hundred percent yours. Employer money can follow a schedule.

lines.text: For a match, the law sets the slowest schedules allowed: a 3-year cliff, or graded from 20% at year 2 to 100% at year 6.
lines.say: For a match, the law sets the slowest schedules allowed: a three-year cliff, or graded from twenty percent at year two to one hundred percent at year six.

lines.text: Example: leave after 4 years on that graded schedule, and you keep 60%: $4,320 of $7,200, ignoring growth.
lines.say: Example: leave after four years on that graded schedule, and you keep sixty percent: four thousand, three hundred twenty dollars of seventy-two hundred, ignoring growth.

lines.text: Many plans vest faster than the legal limit. The actual schedule is in the plan's summary plan description.
lines.say: Many plans vest faster than the legal limit. The actual schedule is written in the plan's summary plan description.

lines.text: Chapter 7: The one-screen recap.
lines.say: Chapter seven: the one-screen recap.

lines.text: Here's the one-screen recap. First, the default: where money lands if nobody picks.
lines.say: Here's the one-screen recap. First, the default: where money lands if nobody picks.

lines.text: Second, expense ratios, which in our hypothetical meant a $67,109 gap.
lines.say: Second, expense ratios, which in our hypothetical meant a sixty-seven thousand, one hundred nine dollar gap.

lines.text: Third, the overall mix. A target-date fund is built to stand alone, and stacking other funds on top changes it.
lines.say: Third, the overall mix. A target-date fund is built to stand alone, and stacking other funds on top of it changes things.

lines.text: Fourth, how much sits in company stock, and when the rules let you move it.
lines.say: Fourth, how much sits in company stock, and when the rules let you move it.

lines.text: Then the money rules: the annual limit, catch-ups and the new Roth rule, the match formula, and the vesting schedule.
lines.say: Then the money rules: the annual limit, catch-ups and the new Roth rule, the match formula, and the vesting schedule.

lines.text: So, is owning one fund lazy? For 61% of Vanguard savers, it's the whole plan. And now you know what's inside it.
lines.say: So, is owning one fund lazy? For sixty-one percent of Vanguard savers, it's the whole plan. And now you know exactly what's inside it.

lines.text: That's the money. Follow for more.
lines.say: That's the money. Follow for more.

post.title: 61% of Vanguard 401(k) savers hold one target-date fund. How to pick 401(k) investments (2026 guide)
post.ig: In 2025, 61% of Vanguard 401(k) savers held a single target-date fund. Here's what's inside it, and what else is on the menu.
post.tiktok: In 2025, 61% of Vanguard 401(k) savers held a single target-date fund. Here's how the whole 401(k) menu works.
post.yt_desc:
A step-by-step guide to the investment menu in a 401(k): what happens if you never choose (the Labor Department's default investment rule and SECURE 2.0 auto-enrollment), how target-date funds and their glide paths work, and what index funds, actively managed funds, stable value and company stock are. It walks through a hypothetical 0.05% versus 0.75% expense ratio example on $50,000 over 30 years ($67,109 gap at an assumed 7% return before fees), plus diversification, rebalancing, the 2026 IRS limits ($24,500, the $8,000 and $11,250 catch-ups, the new Roth catch-up rule above $150,000 in 2025 FICA wages), employer match math and vesting schedules. It ends with a one-screen recap.

CHAPTERS

Sources: Vanguard, How America Saves 2026 (June 2026); IRS Notice 2025-67 (2026 limits and Roth catch-up wage threshold); Treasury/IRS final Roth catch-up regulations (Sept 2025); ICI, The Economics of Providing 401(k) Plans, 2024 (July 2025); ICI, Trends in the Expenses and Fees of Funds, 2025 (March 2026); Morningstar, 2026 Target-Date Landscape; US Department of Labor, QDIA rule (29 CFR 2550.404c-5) and fee disclosure rule (29 CFR 2550.404a-5); IRC 401(a)(35) and 411(a); SECURE 2.0 Act; CNBC (March 30, 2026) on the DOL's proposed fund-selection rule.

News and education, not financial advice.
